text: Given a valid X-Square-Access-Token header, when any tool is called, then the outbound Square request carries Authorization: Bearer <token> and no server-side stored credential is used.
evidence: pytest -v: tests/test_api_client.py::test_access_token_forwarded_as_bearer_auth PASSED (dev/PRD-21318 @ local run, uv run pytest, 30 passed in 1.21s).

text: Given no X-Square-Access-Token header, when POST /mcp tools/call is sent, then the response is 401 listing the required header and zero outbound Square calls are made.
evidence: pytest PASSED. Also confirmed against the real Docker image: `curl -i -X POST /mcp` with no credential header returned `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` and body `{"error":"Missing credentials",...,"required_headers":["X-Square-Access-Token"]}`.

text: Given X-Square-Environment: sandbox, when any tool is called, then the outbound request targets https://connect.squareupsandbox.com/v2; given the header is omitted or 'production', it targets https://connect.squareup.com/v2.
evidence: pytest PASSED.

text: Given X-Square-Environment set to a value other than production or sandbox, when any tool is called, then it returns an invalid_argument error and makes no outbound call.
evidence: pytest PASSED. Also confirmed against the real Docker image: `X-Square-Environment: bogus` returned `{"error":{"code":"invalid_argument","message":"Invalid X-Square-Environment value: 'bogus'; must be 'production' or 'sandbox'.","retryable":false}}` with zero outbound calls.

text: Given two concurrent tools/call requests with two different tokens/environments, when both run at the same time, then each resolves a SquareClient carrying only its own token and base URL.
evidence: pytest PASSED: two concurrent /mcp calls (tenant-a-token/production, tenant-b-token/sandbox) each hit their own base URL with only their own Authorization header.

text: GET /health returns 200 {"status": "ok", ...} with no Square credential configured anywhere.
evidence: pytest PASSED. Also confirmed against the real Docker image: `curl http://127.0.0.1:18080/health` -> `HTTP 200`, body `{"status":"ok","transport":"http","auth_mode":"gateway"}`.

text: A tools/list call with no prior initialize session succeeds with HTTP 200 (stateless Streamable HTTP).
evidence: pytest PASSED. Also confirmed against the real Docker image: a bare `tools/list` POST with a credential header but no prior `initialize` call returned HTTP 200 with the full 12-tool list.

text: square_list_locations calls GET /v2/locations and returns locations with id, name, and status.
evidence: pytest PASSED.

text: square_list_customers with no arguments calls GET /v2/customers and returns a page of customers plus a cursor when more results exist.
evidence: pytest PASSED.

text: square_search_customers with email_address and given_name builds a POST /v2/customers/search filter containing exactly those fields and returns the matches.
evidence: pytest PASSED; asserted the sent JSON body's query.filter equals exactly {email_address, given_name}.

text: square_get_customer with an existing customer_id calls GET /v2/customers/{customer_id} and returns that customer's detail.
evidence: pytest PASSED.

text: square_get_customer with a non-existent customer_id returns a not_found error envelope, not an unhandled exception.
evidence: pytest PASSED.

text: square_list_catalog_items calls GET /v2/catalog/list?types=ITEM (with cursor when provided) and returns catalog items.
evidence: pytest PASSED; asserted outbound query param types=ITEM.

text: square_get_catalog_item returns the object for an existing object_id, and not_found for a non-existent one.
evidence: pytest PASSED (both the existing-id and missing-id branches).

text: square_search_orders builds POST /v2/orders/search with exactly the filters provided (location_ids, state, date filters, cursor) and returns matching orders.
evidence: pytest PASSED; asserted sent body's location_ids, query.filter.state_filter, query.filter.date_time_filter.created_at, and cursor.

text: square_get_order returns the order for an existing order_id, and not_found for a non-existent one.
evidence: pytest PASSED.

text: square_list_payments passes exactly the query parameters provided (location_id, begin_time, end_time, cursor) to GET /v2/payments.
evidence: pytest PASSED; asserted only location_id was present in the sent query params, begin_time/end_time/cursor absent.

text: square_get_payment returns the payment for an existing payment_id, and not_found for a non-existent one.
evidence: pytest PASSED.

text: square_get_inventory_count calls GET /v2/inventory/{catalog_object_id}, passing location_ids as a query filter when provided, and returns current stock counts.
evidence: pytest PASSED; asserted outbound query param location_ids=loc_1.

text: square_create_refund without an idempotency_key generates one, calls POST /v2/refunds, and returns the created refund (id, status, amount_money).
evidence: pytest PASSED; asserted a non-empty idempotency_key was generated and merged into the sent body.

text: Two calls to square_create_refund with the same idempotency_key and arguments produce the same refund result; Square is not treated as having processed two refunds.
evidence: pytest PASSED; both calls sent the same idempotency_key and the tool returned identical text both times (client-side passthrough; Square's own idempotency guarantee is the mocked server's contract here, per Risks & dependencies).

text: Square rejecting a refund (e.g. amount exceeds refundable balance) returns a structured error with Square's upstream code/message, not an unhandled exception.
evidence: pytest PASSED; asserted code=invalid_argument and Square's detail text surfaced in message.

text: A representative 4xx and a representative 5xx response from Square each map to the correct envelope code; a 429 on a read call is retried honoring Retry-After before giving up.
evidence: pytest PASSED for all three; also test_429_succeeds_after_one_retry and test_post_is_never_retried_on_5xx confirm the retry-only-GET policy.

text: End-to-end confirmation against a real Square sandbox account (optional, not blocking per SOP -- missing a vendor test account is not a blocker).
steps: Obtain a real Square sandbox access token with a test location, customer, catalog item, and a completed test payment
Call square_list_locations, square_get_customer, square_get_payment, then square_create_refund for a small amount against that payment
Check the Square sandbox dashboard for the resulting refund
expect: Each read tool returns data matching the sandbox dashboard; the refund appears against the payment with the requested amount.
evidence: No real Square sandbox account is available to DEV01 at dev time either. Not a blocker per SOP (missing vendor test account does not block delivery). As a substitute, the dev leg ran a live network smoke test against production Square with a placeholder token: `square_list_locations` with `X-Square-Access-Token: placeholder-token` reached https://connect.squareup.com/v2/locations for real and received Square's own 401, which this service mapped to the structured envelope {"error":{"code":"unauthorized",...}} -- confirming the full request path (header -> client -> real Square endpoint -> error mapping) works end-to-end; only the token's validity could not be exercised.
